Audit repo /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-55_global-footer-ui, 55 commits ahead of develop.

YOUR SCOPE — TypeScript typing ONLY. Other agents own tokens/CSS, imports, tests, AC conformance.

READ FIRST, in full:
- .claude/rules/typescript.md
- .claude/rules/components.md — the "Components" and "Hooks" sections

AUDIT every .ts/.tsx in `git diff origin/develop --name-only` under overrides/, plus .storybook/preview.tsx.

Check against typescript.md in full: `any` without an inline justification; `type` vs `interface`; non-null assertion `!` without justification; discriminated unions for variant/state modelling; utility types over hand-copied shapes; `import type` for type-only imports; `satisfies` over `as`; `readonly` where the receiver must not mutate; generic parameter naming.

Then components.md: props type name matches component; props type placement; required props non-optional and optional use `?` (no `| undefined` unions); callback props named onEventName; JSDoc on any component with >=2 callers and on every exported hook (with @returns on hooks); typed hook params and explicit hook return types.

ALSO run `npx tsc --noEmit` ONCE for the whole branch and report any errors, cross-referenced to files in scope. Separately note whether `tsconfig.json`'s `include` covers every file this branch modified — if a modified file is outside it, that file is never typechecked, which is itself a finding.

Pay particular attention to these, which are new on this branch and carry security or correctness weight:
- overrides/app/utils/safeHref.ts — an allow-list guard whose result gates whether an href reaches an anchor
- overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.ts — newly extracted, owns focus management and a keyboard trap
- overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx — the largest file; check the SubmitState union, the PendingSignup type, and the new enableNameCapture prop threading
- overrides/app/types/contentful.ts and overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts

ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS:
- Run `git diff origin/develop -- <file>` before flagging; label PRE-EXISTING where the line is not newly added. `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`'s entire diff is 14 comment lines; `_app-config/index.tsx`'s is 2 lines.
- An `any`, `as`, or `!` WITH an adjacent comment explaining why is COMPLIANT per typescript.md. Check for the comment before flagging.
- `vendor.d.ts` is an ambient declaration file for untyped vendor packages; `any` there for genuinely unresolvable vendor types is expected — judge on whether a comment justifies it.
- ALREADY FIXED on this branch, do not re-report unless your analysis differs: the four `as` casts that were on the href-guard path and ZimmNavItem's onClick (removed in 2c4ab7a), and the namedItem cast now keeping `| null`.
- If you propose a type predicate anywhere, check it is SOUND first. `isSafeHref(href): href is string` is UNSOUND — 'javascript:void(0)' is a string that returns false, so the false branch would narrow to `undefined` incorrectly. That was evaluated and deliberately rejected in favour of widening the caller.
- Do not report a proxy as a finding; verify by compiling rather than by reading, where you can.

OUTPUT: findings classified MUST-FIX / SHOULD-FIX / BACKLOG with file:line, plus an explicit "verified compliant" section. Read-only — do not modify files.

# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

content.text:
## Scope & verification method

37 `.ts`/`.tsx` files in `git diff origin/develop` (36 under `overrides/` + `.storybook/preview.tsx`). Every finding below was diffed against `origin/develop` before flagging, and the three load-bearing claims were verified by compiling probe files (created under `overrides/`, run through the project's own `tsconfig.json`, then deleted — `git status` confirmed clean).

## `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean

**Exit 0, zero errors.** Program = 93 in-repo files.

**tsconfig `include` gap (BACKLOG):** `include` is `["overrides/**/*", "vitest.config.ts", "vitest.setup.ts"]`. `.storybook/preview.tsx` is the only modified `.ts`/`.tsx` outside it — confirmed via `tsc --listFilesOnly` (0 `.storybook` files in the program). **It is never typechecked, by `npx tsc --noEmit` or by CI.** I compiled it in isolation (with `vendor.d.ts` added to supply the ambient decls) and it is currently error-free, so this is latent risk, not a hidden break. Both `tsconfig.json` and `.storybook/` are Tier 1 — Integration team, not a feature PR.

---

## MUST-FIX

**1. `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon/index.tsx:140-143` — `as` casts justified by a factually false comment**

```ts
// TypeScript cannot index a discriminated union type directly — each branch must be cast
// individually to access the relevant key without a type error.
const ariaHidden = (aria as { 'aria-hidden'?: boolean })['aria-hidden'];
const ariaLabel = (aria as { 'aria-label'?: string })['aria-label'];
```

I copied this file verbatim, deleted both casts (`aria['aria-hidden']`, `aria['aria-label']`), and compiled under the project tsconfig: **clean.** The stated reason is wrong — TS indexes the rest-destructured XOR union fine. New file on this branch. No runtime impact; the issue is that `typescript.md`'s comment requirement is satisfied only in form, and a wrong justification is worse than none — the "cast is safe here" idiom has already been copied into `zimmInputAction:42` and `footer:92`. The casts also silently widen `'aria-hidden': true` to `boolean` and erase the XOR guarantee.

**2. `overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx:181-182` — unjustified `as` doubling as a hidden non-null assertion**

```ts
const footer = canvasElement.querySelector('footer[role="contentinfo"]') as HTMLElement;
const slot = footer.querySelector('[aria-live]') as HTMLElement;
```

No comment (rule requires one). `querySelector` returns `Element | null`; the cast's real work is asserting non-null, which `typescript.md` treats the same as `!` and says to replace with a null check or early return. `Element` already has `getBoundingClientRect`, so the widening buys nothing. Under `strict: true` the honest form is `querySelector<HTMLElement>(...)` plus a null guard — otherwise a selector miss throws an opaque null TypeError instead of a readable play-function failure. (Overlaps the tests agent on file ownership; the violation itself is typing.)

---

## SHOULD-FIX

**3. `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:104, 125, 126` — mutable arrays in new CMS prop types**

`links: FooterNavLinkEntry[]`, `navGroups: FooterNavGroupEntry[]`, `legalLinks?: FooterNavLinkEntry[]`. These are exactly the case `typescript.md`'s `readonly` rule names — object/array props passed down from a parent that still owns the data. `Footer` only maps over them. Internally inconsistent: this branch's own `BottomBarProps.legalLinks` (`footer/index.tsx:356`) is `ReadonlyArray<...>`. Concrete exposure: `FOOTER_FIXTURE` is a module-level singleton passed as `data`, so any consumer can mutate the shared fixture.

**4. `overrides/app/hooks/useSubscribeModal.ts:16, 18` — `React` type used with no import**

`formRef: React.RefObject<HTMLFormElement>` / `firstFocusRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement>`; line 1 imports only the hooks. Verified by probe that bare `React.X` compiles via the `@types/react` UMD global. Its sibling — added by the same branch — gets it right: `useZimmTextInputState.ts:2` has `import type React from 'react'`. Violates the `import type` rule (type-vs-value not explicit at the import site). Same gap at `useZimmTextInputState.test.ts:14`.

**5. `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts:86-132` — three new hand-copied `sys` envelopes**

`FooterNavLinkEntry`, `FooterNavGroupEntry`, `FooterConfigEntry` each retype `sys: { id: string; contentType: { sys: { id: '...' } } }`. A generic `ContentfulEntry<TContentTypeId extends string, TFields>` collapses all three (and the two pre-existing copies in `HomepageEntry`/`ShoppableImageEntry`). Flagged SHOULD-FIX rather than BACKLOG because this branch triples an existing duplication — though it is following local precedent, so it's DRY-vs-consistency, not a clear-cut error.

---

## BACKLOG

**6. `theme/components/footer.ts:47-84` + `zimmTextInput.ts:68-70` — `parts` has no compile-time link to `baseStyle` or to consumers.** `parts: [...]` (no `as const`) with `baseStyle` typed `Record<string, SystemStyleObject>`; `footer/index.tsx` makes 35 `styles.<part>` reads against an untyped record. **Verified no drift today** — 35 parts declared, 35 used, zero orphans either way — so latent only. `as const` + `Record<(typeof parts)[number], SystemStyleObject>` would catch it. `zimmNavItem.ts` and `button.ts` use `defineStyleConfig` and are typed.

**7. `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts:35` — new `interface History<TState = unknown>`.** `type` is preferred; no declaration merging needed. Mitigating: sits beside the pre-existing `interface Location` in the same ambient block.

**8. `zimmButton/index.tsx:20-33` — union discriminates on an optional tag.** `variant?` on the label arm, `variant: 'icon'` on the icon arm. **Verified sound** for direct JSX: stray `icon` without `variant="icon"`, `variant="icon"` without `icon`, and an icon-only `size` on the label arm are all rejected. The cost is diagnostic quality — `<ZimmButton label="x" icon="phone"/>` reports `Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'ZimmIconType'`. Adding `icon?: never` to `ZimmLabelButtonProps` — the same XOR technique `zimmIcon`'s own props type already uses — yields a clear message; verified by probe. (A spread `{...props}` bypasses excess-property checking entirely; standard TS, not a defect.)

**9. `theme/fontFace.tsx:44-46` — `window as unknown as { Progressive?... }`.** Compliant on the letter (comment present), but "the only option" is inaccurate: `declare global { interface Window { Progressive?: ... } }` in `vendor.d.ts` is idiomatic and removes the double assertion — and `vendor.d.ts` exists precisely for SDK-injected shapes.

**10. `zimmTextInput/index.tsx:8` and `zimmInputAction/index.tsx:9` — `type?: string`.** Both branch on `type === 'email'` (`:103` and `:51`), so a typo silently disables email autocomplete and validation. `React.HTMLInputTypeAttribute` or a narrow union catches it.

**11. `footer/contentfulSchema.placeholder.ts:12-22, 97`** — `type: string` / `linkType: string` where Contentful has a fixed vocabulary (`'Symbol' | 'Boolean' | 'Array' | 'Link'`); literal unions would catch a typo in a schema destined for a live Contentful space. `footerContentTypes: ContentfulContentTypeDef[]` could be `readonly`.

**12. Uncommented `as` in test files** (overlaps the tests agent): `useZimmTextInputState.test.ts:14`, `recipeGuards.test.ts:69, 83`, `fontFace.test.tsx:25, 71`, `zimmTextInput.test.ts:81`. Structural-reflection widening in test-only code is defensible; it just lacks the comment the rule asks for.

---

## PRE-EXISTING — not introduced by this branch

- `vendor.d.ts:90` (`req?: any`), `:103`, `:108`, `:116` — uncommented `any`. Diff confirms only `History` (33-41) and `bundleBasePath` (99) were added. `:140`'s `any` carries a justification.
- `vendor.d.ts:24, 54, 60, 67, 134` — pre-existing `interface` declarations.
- `header/index.tsx:153, 171, 176, 177` — `as` casts. Diff is 14 comment lines only, as stated.
- `_app-config/index.tsx:189, 197, 199` — `as` casts. Diff is 2 lines (`ZimmFontFace` import + JSX).

---

## Verified compliant

- **Zero non-null assertions (`!`)** anywhere in scope — two independent grep patterns, both empty.
- **Zero new `any`** — the only `any` in scope is pre-existing in `vendor.d.ts`.
- **All 16 props types** use `type` (never `interface`), are named `<ComponentName>Props`, and sit at the top of their component file. None needs a `types.ts` — no sibling imports them; stories infer via `StoryObj<typeof X>`.
- **No `| undefined` in any props type.** The two `string | undefined` occurrences are function params: `safeHref.ts:15` and `footer/index.tsx:298`. I re-derived the reasoning at `footer/index.tsx:283-297` and it is correct — `'javascript:void(0)'` is a `string` that returns `false`, so an `href is string` predicate's false branch would narrow to `undefined` incorrectly. Widening the param is the sound choice; I am not proposing a predicate.
- **Callback props** all `onEventName`: `onClose`, `onSubmit`, `onLogoClick`, `onClick`, `onChange`.
- **Both exported hooks** have JSDoc with `@returns` (`useSubscribeModal.ts:21-33`, `useZimmTextInputState.ts:21-32`), typed destructured params, and explicit return types (`UseSubscribeModalReturn`, `UseZimmTextInputStateReturn`).
- **JSDoc on every multi-caller component:** `Footer:407-415`, `FooterContainer:538-548`, `ZimmButton:37-38`, `ZimmIcon:137`, `ZimmLogo:15-19`, `ZimmNavItem:28-30`, `ZimmTextInput:45-53`, `ZimmInputAction:24`, `ZimmFontFace:71`, `isSafeHref:14`.
- **`SubmitState` (`footer:168`)** — a bare string-literal union with no per-state payload. There is no "pile of optional fields" to collapse, so a discriminated union would be over-modelling. Correct as written. **`PendingSignup` (`:172`)** is a plain record in a typed `useRef<PendingSignup>`.
- **`enableNameCapture` threading** — `FooterProps:50` and `SubscribeSectionProps:179`, both `?`, defaulted `false` at `Footer:422` and `SubscribeSection:190`, passed at `:448`. No `| undefined`.
- **Utility types** — `Omit<FooterProps, 'data'>` (`footer:549`) is exactly the rule's intent. `ReadonlyArray` used correctly at `footer:356`.
- **`import type`** correct in `footer/index.tsx:16`, `contentfulFixture.ts:1`, `zimmButton:4`, `zimmInputAction:5`, `theme/zimmTextInput.ts:1`, `preview.tsx:2`, and all 7 story files.
- **Generic naming** — `TState`/`TParams` (vendor.d.ts) are descriptive and T-prefixed; `ContentfulResponse<T>` is a single obvious parameter.
- **`as const` uses are const assertions, not type assertions** — `ICON_MAP` (`zimmIcon:135`), `BP` (`footer.ts:15`), `BORDER`/`BORDER_INVERSE` (`zimmTextInput.ts:11, 21`) — outside the rule. `ICON_MAP` already gets the exhaustiveness `satisfies` would add: `ICON_MAP[type]` at `:139` errors if any `ZimmIconType` member lacks an entry.
- **`safeHref.ts`** — explicit param and return types, JSDoc on both module and export, no assertions, no `any`. Clean.
- **`.storybook/preview.tsx`** — typed `Decorator`/`Preview`, `import type`, no assertions.
- **Already-fixed items confirmed still fixed:** `footer:96-97` `namedItem` casts keep `| null` with a 4-line justification; `zimmInputAction:44` likewise; `ZimmNavItem`'s `onClick` is typed with no cast; the href-guard path carries no casts — `footer:317-320` and `:138-139` pass `href` straight to `chakra.a`, which accepts `string | undefined`.

**Adjacent, other agents' scope (one line, no action from me):** `footer/index.stories.tsx:2` imports `Meta`/`StoryObj` from `@storybook/react` while all six ui-kit stories use `@storybook/react-webpack5` — for the imports agent.
